name: Scrambled eggs on toast
steps: Whisk the eggs with the milk and a pinch of salt and pepper until smooth.
Toast the bread and keep it warm on a plate.
Melt the butter in a nonstick pan over medium-low heat, then pour in the eggs.
Stir slowly with a spatula for 2–3 minutes until the eggs are softly set with no runny liquid left, then spoon onto the toast.

name: French toast
steps: In a shallow dish, whisk the eggs, milk, cinnamon and vanilla together.
Melt half the butter in a large nonstick pan over medium heat.
Dip each slice of bread in the egg mixture for a few seconds per side so it soaks in but doesn't fall apart.
Cook 2–3 minutes per side until golden brown and the center is set, adding the rest of the butter for the second batch.
Serve warm with maple syrup if you like.

name: Fluffy pancakes

ingredients.note: melted, plus extra for the pan

steps: In a bowl, mix the flour, sugar, baking powder and salt.
In another bowl, whisk the milk, egg and melted butter, then pour into the dry ingredients and stir just until combined; a few lumps are fine.
Heat a nonstick pan over medium heat and brush with a little butter.
Pour in about 1/4 cup batter per pancake and cook 2–3 minutes until bubbles form on top and the edges look set.
Flip and cook 1–2 minutes more until golden and cooked through. Serve with maple syrup.

name: Banana oat pancakes
steps: Mash the banana well in a bowl with a fork.
Whisk in the eggs, then stir in the oats, baking powder and cinnamon; let sit 5 minutes to thicken.
Melt a little of the butter in a nonstick pan over medium-low heat.
Spoon in 2 tbsp of batter per pancake and cook 2–3 minutes until the edges are set and the bottom is golden.
Flip gently and cook 1–2 minutes more until cooked through, adding more butter as needed.

name: Overnight oats
steps: In a jar or container, stir together the oats, milk, yogurt and honey.
Cover and refrigerate overnight, or at least 4 hours, so the oats soften.
In the morning, stir, top with berries if using, and eat cold.

name: Apple cinnamon oatmeal
steps: Add the milk, diced apple, cinnamon and a pinch of salt to a saucepan and bring to a gentle simmer over medium heat.
Stir in the oats and lower the heat to medium-low.
Cook 5–7 minutes, stirring often, until the oats are creamy and the apple is soft.
Spoon into bowls and sprinkle with the brown sugar.

name: Breakfast burrito
steps: Whisk the eggs with a pinch of salt.
Warm the black beans in a small pan or the microwave for 1–2 minutes until hot.
Melt the butter in a nonstick pan over medium-low heat, add the eggs and stir for 2–3 minutes until set.
Warm the tortillas in a dry pan or microwave for 20 seconds so they fold without cracking.
Fill each tortilla with eggs, beans, cheese and salsa, fold in the sides and roll up tightly.

name: Huevos rancheros
steps: Warm the black beans in a small saucepan over medium heat for 3–4 minutes, mashing some with a fork; season with salt.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a large pan over medium heat and warm the tortillas about 30 seconds per side; place two on each plate.
Add the remaining oil, crack in the eggs and fry 3–4 minutes until the whites are fully set.
Spread beans on the tortillas, top each with an egg, then spoon over the salsa and sprinkle with cheese.
Add avocado slices on the side if using.

name: Shakshuka
steps: Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the onion and bell pepper and cook 6–8 minutes until soft.
Stir in the garlic, cumin and paprika and cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the tomatoes with a pinch of salt and simmer 8–10 minutes until slightly thickened.
Make 4 small wells in the sauce and crack an egg into each. Cover and cook on medium-low 6–8 minutes until the whites are fully set.
Serve straight from the pan with bread for dipping.

name: Spinach and feta frittata
steps: Heat the oven to 375°F. Whisk the eggs with the milk and a pinch of salt and pepper.
Heat the oil in a 10-inch oven-safe skillet over medium heat. Cook the onion 4–5 minutes until soft, then add the spinach and stir 1 minute until wilted.
Pour in the eggs, scatter the feta on top, and cook without stirring 2–3 minutes until the edges begin to set.
Move the skillet to the oven and bake 12–15 minutes until the center is set and no longer jiggly. Use an oven mitt — the handle is hot. Cool 5 minutes and slice.

name: Egg muffin cups
steps: Heat the oven to 350°F and grease a 12-cup muffin tin with the butter.
Whisk the eggs with the milk and a pinch of salt.
Divide the bell pepper, spinach and cheese among the cups, then pour the egg mixture over, filling each about two-thirds full.
Bake 18–20 minutes until puffed and set in the center. Cool 5 minutes before removing; refrigerate leftovers up to 4 days.

name: Avocado toast with egg
steps: Toast the bread.
Mash the avocado in a bowl with a squeeze of lemon and a pinch of salt.
Heat the oil in a small nonstick pan over medium heat, crack in the egg and fry 3–4 minutes until the white is fully set (flip for 30 seconds if you prefer a firm yolk).
Spread the avocado on the toast, top with the egg, and sprinkle with red pepper flakes.

name: Greek yogurt parfait
steps: Spoon half the yogurt into a glass or bowl.
Add half the berries and half the oats, then repeat the layers.
Drizzle the honey over the top and eat right away so the oats stay crunchy.

name: Peanut butter banana smoothie
steps: Peel the banana and break it into chunks.
Add the banana, peanut butter, milk, yogurt and honey to a blender.
Blend on high for 30–60 seconds until smooth; add a splash more milk if it's too thick, or a few ice cubes if using a fresh banana.

name: Berry smoothie
steps: Add the berries, banana, yogurt and milk to a blender, plus honey if you want it sweeter.
Blend on high for 45–60 seconds until completely smooth.
Add a splash more milk if it's too thick to blend, then pour and serve.

name: Bacon, egg and cheese sandwich
steps: Lay the bacon in a cold skillet, then turn the heat to medium and cook 6–8 minutes, turning occasionally, until crisp. Drain on a paper towel.
Pour off most of the fat, add the butter, crack in the egg and fry 3–4 minutes, flipping once, until the white and yolk are set.
Lay the cheese on the egg for the last 30 seconds so it melts; meanwhile toast the bread.
Stack the egg, cheese and bacon between the toast, add a little pepper, and serve.

name: Breakfast potato hash
steps: Microwave the cubed potatoes in a covered bowl for 4–5 minutes until just tender when poked with a fork.
Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add the potatoes in one layer and cook 6–8 minutes, turning occasionally, until golden and crisp.
Add the onion, bell pepper, paprika and a good pinch of salt and pepper; cook 5–6 minutes more until the vegetables are soft.
If adding eggs, make two wells, crack in the eggs, cover and cook on medium-low 4–5 minutes until the whites are set.

name: Sausage and egg skillet
steps: Cook the sausage in a large skillet over medium-high heat for 7–8 minutes, breaking it up, until browned with no pink left and it reaches 160°F. Move to a plate.
Add the oil and potatoes with a pinch of salt; cover and cook on medium 10–12 minutes, stirring occasionally, until tender and golden.
Add the bell pepper and cook 3 minutes, then return the sausage to the pan.
Make 4 wells, crack in the eggs, cover and cook on medium-low 5–6 minutes until the whites are set. Sprinkle with cheese, cover for 1 minute to melt, and serve.

name: Peanut butter banana toast
steps: Toast the bread until golden.
Spread the peanut butter over the warm toast.
Top with banana slices, then drizzle with honey and sprinkle with cinnamon if you like.

name: Fried egg rice bowl
steps: Reheat the rice in the microwave, covered, for 1–2 minutes until steaming hot, and put it in a bowl.
Heat the vegetable oil in a nonstick pan over medium-high heat, crack in the eggs and fry 2–3 minutes until the edges are crisp and the whites are fully set.
Slide the eggs onto the rice, drizzle with the soy sauce and sesame oil, and scatter the green onions on top.

name: Baked oatmeal
steps: Heat the oven to 375°F and grease an 8x8-inch baking dish with butter.
In a bowl, mix the oats, baking powder, cinnamon and salt.
In another bowl, whisk the milk, eggs, maple syrup and melted butter, then stir into the oat mixture.
Fold in the berries, pour into the dish and spread level.
Bake 35–40 minutes until golden on top and set in the center. Cool 5 minutes, then cut into squares.

name: Cinnamon apple toast
steps: Melt the butter in a small pan over medium heat. Add the apple slices, brown sugar and cinnamon.
Cook 4–5 minutes, stirring now and then, until the apples are soft and lightly caramelized.
Meanwhile toast the bread, then pile the warm apples on top and spoon over any pan juices.

name: Ham and cheese omelette
steps: Whisk the eggs with a pinch of salt and pepper.
Melt the butter in a nonstick pan over medium heat and warm the ham for 1–2 minutes.
Spread the ham out, pour in the eggs, and lower the heat to medium-low. Gently push the edges toward the center as they set, tilting so raw egg runs underneath.
When the eggs are set with no runny liquid on top, sprinkle the cheese over one half, fold, and slide onto a plate.

name: Spinach scramble
steps: Whisk the eggs with a pinch of salt and pepper.
Heat the oil in a nonstick pan over medium heat. Add the garlic and cook 30 seconds, then add the spinach and stir 1–2 minutes until wilted.
Lower the heat to medium-low, pour in the eggs and stir gently for 2–3 minutes until softly set with no runny liquid.
Sprinkle with parmesan if using and serve.

name: Egg in a hole
steps: Cut a round hole about 2 inches wide in the center of the bread using a glass or cookie cutter.
Melt the butter in a nonstick pan over medium heat and add the bread and the cut-out circle.
Crack the egg into the hole, season with salt and pepper, and cook 2–3 minutes until the bottom is golden and the white starts to set.
Flip carefully and cook 1–2 minutes more until the white is fully set (longer for a firm yolk). Serve with the toasted circle.

name: Breakfast quesadilla
steps: Whisk the eggs with a pinch of salt. Melt the butter in a nonstick pan over medium-low heat and scramble the eggs 2–3 minutes until set; move to a plate.
Wipe the pan, lay the tortilla in it and sprinkle half of it with half the cheese, then the eggs, then the rest of the cheese.
Fold the tortilla over and cook on medium heat 2–3 minutes per side until golden and crisp and the cheese is melted.
Cut into wedges and serve with the salsa.
